solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Son has to acquire money for a bet

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in family trees
to take something is to acquire it

explanation.surface: A boy has to find some cash before he can place a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler's wagered sum, the amount put at risk on an outcome, is called this.

clue.text: Just using cunning when catching little devil

indicators.note: the word for cunning takes the little devil inside it

parts.note: a cunning person is sly
an imp is a small mischievous devil

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to trickery only when trapping a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely or only: 'it is just a test' means it is no more than a test.

clue.text: Article naming word to fix statement

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a noun is the part of speech that names a thing
to cement something is to fix it firmly in place

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: how to settle on the right word in a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A public or formal declaration, such as one made by a spokesperson, is this.

clue.text: Listening device open, hear poorly

indicators.note: the words are put together badly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with bad hearing is told to open up and use a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A small speaker worn on or in the ear, as with a radio or phone, is this listening aid.

clue.text: Get back with Royal Engineers over military takeover

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a coup is a seizure of power by the army

explanation.surface: Army engineers regain control after soldiers seize the government.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or regain, as lost money or strength, is to get it back.

clue.text: Starts to employ dogs guarding European border

indicators.note: the starts, the opening letters, of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone begins using guard dogs to patrol a European frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guarding' looks like an instruction to put one piece inside another, but its first letter is simply one of the three taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim or margin, the outer line of something, is a synonym of border.

clue.text: Reported vendor offering stock of wine

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word for vendor is heard rather than written

parts.note: a vendor is someone who sells, a seller

explanation.surface: A merchant is said to be offering a supply of wine for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine collection kept in storage, as in 'he has a fine one', is called by the name of its underground room.

clue.text: Bad enamel breaking up is open to being put right

indicators.note: enamel that is breaking up falls apart, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Damaged tooth enamel that is cracking can still be fixed by a dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like it describes the enamel, but it is part of the letters to rearrange; 'breaking up' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something capable of correction or alteration, as a draft law or text, can be amended.

clue.text: Vigorously hearty rugby players drinking like animals

parts.note: the backs are the rugby players positioned behind the forwards
cats and dogs drink by lapping with the tongue

explanation.surface: Boisterous rugby players knock back their drinks like beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusively jovial, with much patting of others' shoulders in congratulation, as in a club bar.

clue.text: Mine ore endlessly that's inferior

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its final letter, so neither has an end

explanation.surface: A miner grumbles that extracting rock without end yields only poor stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' works on both words: MIN(E) and OR(E).
explanation.definitionFit: Lesser, smaller or lower in rank: a junior or subordinate thing is described this way.

clue.text: Demonstrated calibre briefly in French language

parts.note: something demonstrated has been shown to be true, i.e. proven

indicators.note: the word calibre is cut short, keeping only its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Someone showed real quality, in a concise way, in a language spoken in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occitan dialect of Provence in southern France, the tongue of the troubadours, goes by this name.

clue.text: Money we earn in eastern parts?

definitions.text: Money we earn in eastern parts?

parts.words: Money we earn in eastern parts
parts.note: the clue describes the currency of Japan, a country in the Far East; 'we earn' also suggests a yearning, the word's other sense

explanation.surface: A question about the wages people are paid in Asian countries.
explanation.walkthrough: The currency of Japan is the yen; the word also means a longing, which 'we earn' hints at by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Japanese unit of currency, the money earned by workers in the Far East.

clue.text: Nought prospers with reforming tyrant

parts.note: nought is zero, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: reforming means forming again in a new shape, so the letters of prospers are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nobody grows rich by pushing through reforms, and turns into a despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot or cruel ruler who keeps people down by harsh, unjust use of power is called this.

clue.text: Former partner was likely to be drawn out

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
if something tended to happen it was likely to

explanation.surface: An ex-spouse was apt to be long-winded.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthened or prolonged, as a stay or a meeting that goes on, is a synonym.

clue.text: Repented being wrong about a key earlier legal case

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the musical key
the letters of repented are put the wrong way round, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: C is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Someone said sorry for being in error about something important, citing an earlier court ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being wrong' rearranges REPENTED, and 'about' puts that around C, one of the musical keys.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a prior judgment that guides how later similar disputes are decided is cited as this.

clue.text: Left in charge after bar's open

indicators.note: the left-in-charge pieces come after the bar in the answer

parts.note: a bar is a pub; the 's stands for 'is', joining the pieces

explanation.surface: Someone is left to run things once the pub has opened its doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' looks like part of the pub story but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Accessible to all, not private: a session that is not secret is this.

clue.text: Superhero, tickled, keeps arousing excitement

indicators.note: the answer is kept within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A comic-book hero, amused, keeps getting people worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Of sexual desire: something sensual that stirs or rouses passion is described this way.

clue.text: Beer is light with no head

indicators.note: the word for light loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a light colour is a pale one

explanation.surface: A claim that a drink is weak, lacking a frothy top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beer is light' invites a light ale; but light means PALE, which loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional brewed malt drink, such as bitter, is a type of this.

clue.text: Head of corn belonging to you once covered in soil

parts.note: an ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant
thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: An old harvest image: the corn you once owned now lies buried in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty with mud or tasting of the ground, as a freshly dug potato would be.

clue.text: Failure of short holiday away from university

parts.note: a brief trip away, such as a weekend break
students who have gone down have left Oxford or Cambridge, at the end of term or for good

explanation.surface: A student's brief vacation off campus ends in disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage, going down means leaving a university such as Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse or stoppage, as of a car or of negotiations, is called this.

clue.text: Gentle sort

definitions.meaning: a type or category, as in 'of that ...'

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means benevolent and caring; as a noun it means a type or variety.

clue.text: Go with the current meaning

definitions.meaning: to be carried along by a flow of water or air
the general sense or gist of what is said, as in 'catch my ...'

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means float along passively; as a noun it means the gist or point of what someone says.

clue.text: Playing tennis I have concentrated

indicators.note: the letters of tennis are put into play, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: I have contracts to I've

explanation.surface: Someone says that while playing a sport they have been fully focused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges TENNIS to INTENS; I've, the short form of 'I have', supplies IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort that is focused and thorough, packed into a short time, is described this way.

clue.text: Like, maybe, a setter's party — good and extremely gay

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of gay are used

explanation.surface: The puzzle's compiler hosts a celebration that is fine and very cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is not the puzzle compiler but a dog breed, such as an Irish setter.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a gun dog, so something resembling a setter's would be canine in character.
